title: The fourth view states only what is certain: predictions are true, and the infinite intellect reaches all truth
source_text: XL. Quod spectat autem quartam sententiam, quae divinae praescientiae certitudinem quaerit in infinitate intellectus divini, & in determinata veritate eorum quae contingenter futura sunt, nihil illa ponit quod certum non sit & indubitatum. Nam quandoquidem evidens est, divinas praedictiones de futuris contingentibus in scripturis extare, hoc ipso manifestum est, veras propositiones de iis formari posse: nec enim quicquam Deus affirmat nisi verum. Omni autem verae propositioni necesse est ut in re veritas respondeat. Et sic cum determinate & vere dici possit, haec & illa libere & contingenter futura, consequens est, ut eorum veritas determinata sit. Nec minus est evidens, posita veritate futurorum contingentium, illam ab intellectu divino, qui infinitus est, percipi & cognosci. Nam cum verum sit objectum intellectus, intellectus infinitus ad omne verum se extendit: alioquin hoc ipso infinitus non esset, sed limites & finem haberet, quippe qui non posset aliquam veritatem attingere.
pass_a_gloss: XL. But as regards the fourth opinion, which seeks the certainty of divine foreknowledge in the infinity of the divine intellect, and in the determinate truth of those things which are contingently future, it posits nothing which is not certain and undoubted. For since it is evident, that divine predictions concerning future contingents exist in the scriptures, by this very thing it is manifest, that true propositions can be formed concerning them: for God affirms nothing but what is true. But to every true proposition it is necessary that truth correspond in the thing. And thus since it can be said determinately and truly, that this and that is freely and contingently future, it is consequent, that their truth is determinate. Nor is it less evident, the truth of future contingents being posited, that it is perceived and known by the divine intellect, which is infinite. For since the true is the object of the intellect, an infinite intellect extends itself to every truth: otherwise by this very thing it would not be infinite, but would have limits and end, as one which could not attain some truth.
pass_b_english: The fourth view looks for the certainty of God's foreknowledge in the infinity of the divine intellect and in the determinate truth of things that will happen contingently. It asserts nothing that is not certain and beyond doubt.

It is clear that Scripture contains divine predictions about future contingents. That alone shows that true propositions can be framed about them, for God asserts nothing that is not true. Every true proposition must have truth corresponding to it in reality. So, since it can be said determinately and truly that this or that will happen freely and contingently, it follows that its truth is determinate.

It is no less clear that, once the truth of future contingents is granted, that truth is perceived and known by the divine intellect, which is infinite. Truth is the object of the intellect, so an infinite intellect reaches to all truth. Otherwise it would by that very fact not be infinite but would have bounds and an end, since it could not reach some truth.
